name: Longer Ray5 40W
tagline: 40W Compact fixed-focus diode: simple desk engraver for small projects
tldr: Longer Ray5 40W is the 40W SKU on the Longer longer ray5 line. Longer's compact Ray5 20W diode engraver: verify you are buying the 20W SKU, not the 5W, 10W, or 40W Ray5 listings. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.

priceRange.note: Official Longer store, Oct 2026: $680 to $950 depending on bundle

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Redesigned frame with 15 mm industrial rail and 24,000 mm/min, per Longer
Fills at ~60–130 mm/s: a 10 × 10 cm photo in ~12–18 min
Longer claims thin stainless steel (0.15 mm) can be cut in one pass
cons: Wide 0.10 × 0.15 mm spot: the least detailed Ray5 for small text and portraits
Longer's store price ($679.99 basic in October 2026) sits above our tracked range
Smaller 385 × 385 mm workspace than the older Ray5 frame, per Longer
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 40W SKU on Longer Ray5. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Treat engraving and cutting as separate profiles. Push cut speeds only after test squares on your material. Compare CO₂ only when clear acrylic or all-day production enters the picture.
mainObjective: Maximum cut speed and depth in the line: engraving remains strong at tuned speeds

editorialDepth.advantages: Longer Ray5 40W targets mixed engraving and wood-cutting weeks: fewer passes on basswood and dark acrylic than weaker SKUs in the same line.
editorialDepth.limitations: Wrong pick if you never engrave and only wanted the lowest price. Ultra-fine photo work can look better on an engraving-first SKU. Open-frame: safety and smoke are on you.

faq.question: Is the Ray5 40W the same machine as the other Ray5 models?
faq.answer: No. Longer describes a redesigned frame: 8-beam compressed diode with a 0.10 × 0.15 mm spot, 15 mm industrial rail with a 4-roller Y axis, up to 24,000 mm/min, a 385 × 385 mm workspace and 5.73 kg. Only the name and the general layout are shared with the lower-power Ray5.

faq.question: What does the Ray5 40W cut?
faq.answer: Longer claims 20 mm basswood and 0.15 mm stainless steel in one pass. In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 6–10 min at 3–8 mm/s, and around 10 mm basswood is realistic in passes. Clear acrylic remains impossible.

faq.question: Is it worth the price over the Ray5 20W?
faq.answer: Longer's own store listed the 40W at $679.99 (Basic), $739.99 (Pro) and $949.99 (Pro Max) in October 2026, above our $449–649 tracked range, so compare resellers. It is worth it if you cut weekly: our 3 mm benchmark drops from about 9–15 min to 6–10 min and fills run several times faster.

standoutFeatures.title: Stiffer motion system
standoutFeatures.body: A 15 mm industrial rail and 4-roller Y axis, according to Longer, for steadier cuts at speed.

standoutFeatures.title: Cutting-first power
standoutFeatures.body: 3 mm basswood squares in about 6–10 min in our benchmarks, with around 10 mm reachable in passes.

standoutFeatures.title: Light for its power
standoutFeatures.body: 5.73 kg according to Longer, easy to move between a workbench and storage.
